topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Hidden Logic
target_audience: High school students or introductory computer science learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
lecture_lines: Binary uses only two: zero and one.
Think of bits as light switches.
animations: Create Text "Our world uses ten digits." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display digits 0-9 in a row at center-left.

Create Text "Binary uses only two: zero and one." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display bit '0' and '1' in blue (#3498DB) at center, positioned via self.place_at_grid(obj, 'C5', scale_factor=1.2).

Create Text "Think of bits as light switches." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Animate bit '0' to '1' using a switch visual effect in yellow (#F1C40F), positioned via self.place_in_area(obj, 'A4', 'F6', scale_factor=1.5).

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
lecture_lines: Smaller disks must stay above larger ones.
Move all disks to the final rod.
animations: Create Text "Three rods hold stacked disks." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display three in red (#E74C3C) on the first, positioned via self.place_in_area(rods, 'B3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.85).
Create Text "Smaller disks must stay above larger ones." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show an invalid move attempt flashed in red (#E74C3C) and correct stacking of in green (#2ECC71).

Create Text "Move all disks to the final rod." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Animate moving from start to final using a step-by-step path in purple (#9B59B6), positioned via self.place_at_grid(disk_stack, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8).

sections.title: The Binary Connection
lecture_lines: Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one.
Binary numbers reveal the next move.
Each bit corresponds to a specific disk.
animations: Create Text "Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display formula 2^{n}-1 using MathTex in white (#FFFFFF), positioned via self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=0.7).

Create Text "Binary numbers reveal the next move." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display binary sequence 000 to 111 changing rhythmically below disks represented by, positioned via self.place_at_grid(binary_val, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8).

Create Text "Each bit corresponds to a specific disk." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Use color-coded arrows linking binary bits in blue (#3498DB) to specific, positioned via self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.9).

sections.title: Visualizing the Algorithm
lecture_lines: Changing bits dictate each disk shift.
Small disks move frequently, large ones slowly.
animations: Create Text "Watch the binary rhythm unfold." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show a binary counter ticking up from 000 to 111 alongside the disk, positioned via self.place_in_area(animation_group, 'A2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6).

Create Text "Changing bits dictate each disk shift." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Highlight the changing bit in gold (#F39C12) whenever a disk moves, positioned via self.place_in_area(grid_visual, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5).

Create Text "Small disks move frequently, large ones slowly." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Show smallest disk moving at high frequency and largest at low frequency, positioned via self.place_in_area(lecture_text, 'A1', 'C1', scale_factor=0.9).

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Computers use this for memory management.
animations: Create Text "Recursion simplifies complex problems." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Fade in 2^{n}-1 move summary in cyan (#1ABC9C), positioned via self.place_in_area(formula, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2).

Create Text "Binary logic guides efficient systems." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Display a logic gate diagram flowing with binary bits in green (#2ECC71), positioned via self.place_in_area(box, 'B4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9).

Create Text "Computers use this for memory management." in white (#FFFFFF) at top-center. Overlay an abstract memory block diagram visualizing data movement in purple (#9B59B6) alongside, positioned via self.place_in_area(tree_group, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0).
